sections.h2: Which Falmouth offices deal with tax on a Pendleton County house?
sections.html:
A sale touches three offices in Falmouth. Bills come from the sheriff, values come from the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), and the deed goes to the county clerk, who also takes over any bill that turns delinquent. Pendleton County's website links out to the PVA's own page for parcel lookups and exemption forms.

  • Sheriff: 202 Chapel Street, with tax calls taken at 859-654-4511.
  • County Clerk: Room 1 at 233 Main Street, box 112, Falmouth 41040, telephone 859-654-3380. Weekday service runs 8:30 to 4:00. Saturday service falls on the second and last Saturday of a month, 8:30 until noon, except around holidays.
  • Planning and Zoning: answers for Falmouth and the unincorporated county on floodplains, addresses, code enforcement and plan review.

Statements go to the owner only. Lenders are left off the mailing, so an escrow customer should ask the servicer whether it has a copy.

sections.h2: What dates and amounts apply to the 2026 Pendleton tax bill?
sections.html:
The 2026 statements were mailed on September 30, 2026, in plain envelopes that carry blue lettering reading "2026 Pendleton County Tax Statement." The sheriff asks owners still waiting on October 12 to call. Payment is taken in cash, by check, or on a debit or credit card, though cards add a convenience fee and American Express is refused.

The third column applies the sheriff's percentages to a round number. Counter service stops on county and state holidays and the weekends beside them, such as Veterans Day, Thanksgiving week, Christmas week, New Year's, Martin Luther King Day and the afternoon of Good Friday. The front door has a drop box under video watch. A check left there should include the stub cut from the top of the bill and a phone number, and a stamped return envelope brings back a receipt. Never put cash in it.

sections.h2: How do appeals and the homestead exemption work in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
Disputes start with a visit to the PVA or a deputy. After that, the owner files at the clerk's office by the workday following the end of public roll inspection, which begins the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. At the hearing, paper wins: insurance policies, construction costs and comparable listings.

Homeowners aged 65 or older, and those classed as totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption. It removes $49,100 from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years. On a house at the county's $159,800 Census median, $110,700 stays taxable. Applications go to the PVA.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Pendleton County tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax is a lien that outlasts a sale, with KRS 134.015(5) allowing up to eleven years. The title search at closing finds it, and the payoff is subtracted from what the seller receives.

When April 15 passes, the sheriff hands the bill to the clerk, interest starts at one percent for each month, and Revenue adds a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent attorney charge. The clerk's site links to a list of advertised delinquent bills. A seller who has fallen behind should ask the clerk for a written payoff before agreeing to a contract. If an outside investor buys the certificate first, the debt is owed to that investor with more fees attached.

sections.h2: What will the seller pay the Pendleton County Clerk at closing?
sections.html:
Kentucky charges the grantor fifty cents for every $500 of declared value (KRS 142.050), and the clerk collects before recording. At the county's $159,800 median value the figure rounds to 320 units, so the tax is $160.00.

  • A deed is $50.00 to record, with $3.00 more per page beyond five.
  • A mortgage is $80.00, and releasing one is $46.00.
  • A deed needs a sworn consideration statement from both parties, plus an address where the next tax bill can be sent (KRS 382.135).
  • Spousal transfers and foreclosure deeds are among the exemptions.

The clerk's schedule says prices vary slightly, so call 859-654-3380 for an exact total before the closing date. Before the day arrives, ask the sheriff on Chapel Street whether the current-year bill is paid, and ask the clerk whether any delinquent certificate sits against the parcel. Bring the tax statement itself to the title company so the proration can be figured from the actual amount.

sections.h2: What is Pendleton County's history and geography?
sections.html:
Pendleton County was formed in 1798 out of Campbell and Bracken counties and took its name from Edmund Pendleton, a Virginia jurist. Falmouth started around 1776 as a hamlet called Forks of Licking, won a charter in 1793 and saw one of the state's earliest sawmills that year. Its courthouse was built in 1848. The railroad created Butler about 1852, and the town incorporated in 1868. During the Civil War, Falmouth hosted a Union recruiting camp from September 1861.

The county measures about 280 square miles, with the Ohio River forming part of its northeastern boundary. Falmouth sits where the Main and South Licking rivers meet, and Butler is ten miles north along the Licking. Kincaid Lake State Park offers 850 acres of camping, golf and swimming. Because the planning office handles floodplain rules, a house near the Licking should have its flood zone confirmed before listing. The school list includes Pendleton County High School, Sharp Middle School, Northern Elementary in Butler and Southern Elementary in Falmouth. The county library at 801 Robbins Avenue offers public computers and a bookable meeting room, and the Fryer House, an 1811 stone home, belongs to the Pendleton County Historical Society. Annual events include the Kentucky Wool Festival, and the Griffin Center Amphitheater and Kincaid Regional Theatre host performances. Falmouth native Phillip Allen Sharp won the 1993 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, and the middle school bears his name.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about housing in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists these figures for Pendleton County:

  • 14,800 residents in July 2025, up about 1.1% from the April 2020 base.
  • 6,341 housing units, with owners living in 74.7% of homes.
  • A median owner-occupied value of $159,800 and median gross rent of $793.
  • Monthly owner costs of $1,172 with a mortgage and $475 without one.
  • Median household income of $64,669 and a mean commute of 36.4 minutes.

The 2020 count found 5,533 households and 6,263 housing units, 11.7% of them vacant. About a quarter of households, 24.7%, were one person living alone, and every resident was counted as rural. The Census Bureau recorded zero building permits for 2025, and county population has hovered near 14,000 to 15,000 since 2000. The 2020 census put the median age at 41.6, and QuickFacts shows 19.9% of residents aged 65 or older in 2025, which matters because the homestead exemption starts at 65.

faqs.q: When did Pendleton County mail its 2026 tax bills?
faqs.a: September 30, 2026. The sheriff asks owners without a statement by October 12 to call 859-654-4511.

faqs.q: How large is the late charge after January in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: It is 21% from February 1 to April 15, 2027. Bills settled in January 2027 take a 5% penalty.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's office in Room 1 at 233 Main Street, Falmouth. Hours are weekdays 8:30 to 4:00, plus 8:30 to noon on the second and last Saturday.

faqs.q: Who bears the Kentucky transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor. A sale valued at the $159,800 Census median owes $160.00.

faqs.q: Is a PVA conference required before a Pendleton County appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. The owner meets the PVA or a deputy first, then files with the clerk by the workday after the inspection period closes.
